govdocs-archive_org-mda-mdma-and-other-m: Torsten Passie and Udo Benzenhöfer’s study of MDA, MDMA, and other ‘mescaline-like’ substances in the US military examines the army’s drug tests. The scholars’ pages document secret experiments. Edgewood Arsenal was the test site. The book is a disturbing record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LorenzMarita_Lo: This Vanity Fair piece — The Spy Who Loved Castro — covers Marita Lorenz. Lorenz was Castro’s lover turned CIA asset. Her story was wild. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MilitaryAssista: This item — International Defense Commitments of the United States, Dean Rusk — is a State Department file. Rusk was Kennedy’s Secretary of State. The file endures. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MusgroveRita_Mu: This letter to Ed — July 8, 1974, creator unknown — is a personal note. Letters capture voices the record misses. The note may hold a clue. The file belongs to the personal archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
obiter-dicta: Augustine Birrell's Obiter Dicta — things said by the way — gathers his witty literary essays. His talk of books and authors charmed Victorian readers. The perfect bedside book for book lovers. Lamb, Browning, and other favorites sparkle in his easy essays.
texas-a-brief-account-of-the-origin-prog: William Wharton gives a brief account of Texas — its origin, progress, and present state as a colonial settlement. Written to draw settlers, it is buoyant with promise. A foundational Texas document. Stephen Austin's colony and the fight for freedom fill his stirring pages.
the-naturalist-in-la-plata: W. H. Hudson's Naturalist in La Plata records Argentine birds, beasts, and pampas life with a poet's eye and a scientist's patience. His South American classic stands beside Darwin's own journal of the Beagle voyage. Wonderful natural history, beautifully written.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-grot: This article covers Grottaferrata, the Greek-rite abbey by Rome. St. Nilus founded it a thousand years ago. Douglas Raymund Webster honors its Eastern ways. East and West meet in its choir. Its monks still chant in Greek on feast days.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alessandro-vo: This 1913 reference piece on Alessandro Volta — the inventor of the electric battery. Michael O'Reilly praises his Catholic faith. His pile lit the modern age. The volt bears his immortal name. Science's obedient son of the Church. His letters show a devout Catholic mind.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andres-urdane: A 1913 entry on Andrés Urdaneta — the Augustinian who found the Pacific way home. Camillus Crivelli honors his navigation. His tornaviaje saved the Manila trade. The friar who mapped the ocean. Spain's sailing monk. His charts guided the galleons home.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aosta: A 1913 entry on Aosta — the Alpine diocese of the valley. John Joseph A'Becket gives its Roman story. Its bishops date from antiquity. The great St. Bernard guards its passes. A see among the snows. Its arch of Augustus spans the road.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apophthegmata: This 1913 reference piece on the Apophthegmata — the sayings of the Desert Fathers. Abbot Butler gathers their wisdom. The monks' short words pierce the heart. The desert bloomed with holiness. The Fathers' book of counsel. Their wit instructs the modern reader.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augusta: This 1913 reference article on Augusta — a name in the ancient church story. Thomas Shahan records what is known. The entry preserves its modest fame. The old lists keep its bishops. A see of the ancient empire. Its ruins await the archaeologist's spade.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedict-levi: A 1913 entry on Benedict Levita — the forger of the False Decretals. Johann Peter Kirsch unmasks his pious fraud. His capitularies fooled the Middle Ages. The scholars at last exposed him. The most famous forger of the Church. His forgeries shaped the medieval law.
